lesson_title: Micro Essentials: Four Markets on One Street
hook_text: Your whole micro syllabus is trading on one township street. Come walk it.
clip_script: Walk the street and you pass every market structure in the syllabus. The fruit sellers outside the station: same bananas, same price, nobody can charge a rand more — perfect competition, flat demand line, and when margins fatten, new tables appear and melt the profit back to normal. The water utility: one network of pipes, no rival, output where marginal cost meets marginal revenue and the price read up on demand — the monopoly a regulator must watch. The fuel stations and the banks: the few, watching each other like taxi associations on a shared route — raise alone and lose customers, cut and get matched — so they fight with loyalty cards instead. That sticky price is the kinked demand curve. And the spazas: each slightly its own thing — late hours, the good bread, trust for regulars — monopolistic competition, where every trick gets copied two doors down. Then the corner where the market drops the ball: soapy runoff in the stream, too little studying, no streetlight — tax the harm, subsidise the spillover, build the light. One street. Every graph. Go collect its marks.
visual_style: A hand-drawn township high street scrolling past: fruit tables with a flat price line floating above, water pipes branching from one tower, fuel stations eyeing each other, spaza shops each with a glowing specialty; then a stream turning grey and a streetlight switching on as the fixes stamp in.
mood: Warm, local, eye-opening — the syllabus hiding in plain sight.
pacing: A walking rhythm, one beat per market, slowing at the failure corner, ending on the lit street.
call_to_action: Take the full walk — the whole micro half of the subject in one revision session.
